This information should complete our outstanding requirements as outlined in the Faxed Memorandum sent
by the Director of Air Traffic, AAT-1, dated October 8, 2003. This Memorandum will provide you with an
update on the request to interview all employees that worked on September 11, 2001.

Commission was given copies of all information requested from those files. The Center felt that
the Commission was confused about the difference between an accident package and an accident
file. The Commission had questions about controller statements and was provided copies of all
controller statements. The facility felt they met all of the Commission requests.
Spoke with Cindy Coram, Acting AGL-505. The Commission did not receive the entire accident

They asked Mr. Jones to go through the file and provide copies of all pertinent data. Mr. Jones
provided copies of QA bulletins, facility lessons learned paper, printed sector maps with
frequencies. Some of the data they requested was not released due to guidance from ANE legal
regarding information on hold by the FBI. The Commission was told that release of further
information could be accomplished making a request through the proper channels. Regional
materials that, for whatever reason, were not produced to the Commission. Let me first
review some of the Commission's pertinent document requests, and then address where
we go from here.
I. Requests
On May 7, 2003, the Commission submitted to the Department of Transportation a
request seeking "All documents related to the FAA's tracking of hijacked airliners on
9/11/01, including without limitation communications with NORAD." These documents
were due to the Commission on May 14, 2003.
As the Commission became more familiar with the events of the day and the FAA's air
traffic control system, it submitted additional requests for specific items, including the
following:
( 1) Any document -- whether in draft or final form -- prepared by DOT, the FAA, any of
their components, or any of their employees as after-action or other evaluations ofthe
department's or agency's response to the events of September 11, 2001. This request
includes, but is not limited to, all documents prepared by Steve Brown regarding the ATC
response to 9/11101. (DOT Request No.2, Item 3)
(3) All logs, tapes, and transcripts ofFAA communications with NORAD on the
morning of9/11/01. (DOT Request No.2, Item 16)
( 4) All logs, tapes, and transcripts of internal FAA communications, including
interphone conversations among FAA locations, concerning aircraft presumed to be
hijacked on 9/11/01. (DOT Request No.2, Item 19)
As you can see, these requests specifically targeted after-action reports, interview reports,
tapes of communications with NORAD, and all tapes of internal FAA communications
on 9/11. Inclusion of these specific requests in no way, however, modified our original
request seeking "all documents" related to the FAA's tracking of hijacked airliners.
Much to our surprise, the managers and quality assurance officials at each of the four
centers we visited (ZBW, ZNY, ZID, ZOB) told us they were never asked to gather these
materials for the Commission. At each facility we interviewed both the quality assurance
manager and the air traffic manager. We asked what was the available universe of
documents related to 9/11 (i.e., what lines were recorded? what documents were
produced? were they retained?) and whether anyone from headquarters had ever asked
the Centers to produce these materials to the Commission. Across the board the answer
was no. It is now the middle of October -- with our deadline looming - and we are still
mired in the discussion over access to documents requested in May.
Where do we go from here? In short, our original document request stands as written.
The Commission is seeking "All documents related to the FAA's tracking ofhijacked
airliners on 911110 1." Obviously, the FAA is in a better position to know the universe of
materials related to these flights than are we at the Commission. Having said that, here
are some examples of items we are seeking:
(1) "Accident File" versus "Accident Package": The Commission hereby requests the
complete "accident file" --not the "accident package" --related to the events of 9/11.
That means that if Boston has three boxes of materials related to 9/11, we want
everything in all three boxes. Moreover, this request applies to all FAA air traffic
facilities, not just the four centers we visited.
(2) After Action Reports: The Commission hereby requests any document that
summarizes, describes, evaluates or assesses the FAA's performance in tracking and
responding to the hijackings of 9/11. So, for example, the document that the Air Traffic
Manager at Cleveland wrote and sent to the Great Lakes Regional Office would clearly
fall under this heading. Similarly, any materials related to the outside contractor the Air
Traffic Manger at Indianapolis hired to assess the lapse of radar coverage tracking Flight
77 would qualify. Finally, the Satoris that each center produced reconstructing the
hijacked flights would clearly fall under this category.
As I have emphasized before, this request is not limited to a global comprehensive report
that I understand the air traffic division never produced. We are looking for anything that
was produced by anyone within the FAA evaluating the air traffic performance that
day.
(3) Tapes: The Commission hereby requests any and all tapes related to the FAA's
tracking of the hijacked airliners on 9/11101. That means all communications by FAA air
traffic mangers and other personnel to others within the FAA, in the military, and at the
airlines. Having familiarized ourselves with these facilities and the people involved, I am
confident this is an achievable request that does not entail the review of 3000+ phone
lines. I suggest that we have a meeting or conference call ASAP with the entities
involved in this enterprise, and specifically go through the recording tasks at each
facility.
Finally, let me reiterate that the aforementioned three categories are merely examples of
responsive evidence that the Commission is lacking. I look forward to working with you
to expeditiously resolve these matters. Dana.
